answer: HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, descriptive association): Among black NLSY79 respondents, having been incarcerated (ever_jailed, 1985–1994) is associated with lower subsequent wealth and smaller wealth accumulation, and this association is strongest for individuals with HIGHER baseline (1985) wealth/economic standing. Concretely, the mean 1985→1996 wealth shortfall of the jailed group relative to the non-jailed group within each 1985-wealth tier rises monotonically: low-wealth tier gap ≈ $17,483 (jail n=76), mid-wealth tier ≈ $29,391 (jail n=39), high-wealth tier ≈ $59,008 (jail n=44). In the high-wealth tier the jailed group even shows a mean NEGATIVE 1985→1996 change (≈ −$4,248) while the non-jailed group gains ≈ +$54,760. This is an association, not a causal estimate; the jailed group is heavily male (83–98%) and starts from lower baseline wealth, so selection/confounding cannot be ruled out.

payload.hypothesis: Among black NLSY79 respondents, incarceration (ever jailed 1985-1994) is associated with lower subsequent wealth and smaller 1985-1996 wealth accumulation, and this association is strongest for those with higher baseline (1985) wealth/economic standing. The mean 1985-to-1996 wealth shortfall of the jailed vs non-jailed group rises monotonically across 1985-wealth tertiles: low tier ~$17.5k (jail n=76), mid tier ~$29.4k (jail n=39), high tier ~$59.0k (jail n=44); in the high-wealth tier the jailed group shows a mean NEGATIVE 1985-1996 change (~-$4.2k) while non-jailed gain ~+$54.8k. This is a descriptive association, not a causal estimate: the jailed group is heavily male (83-98%) and starts from lower baseline wealth, so selection/confounding cannot be ruled out.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 6 cols, 0 missing). Confirmed NO income/income-bracket/asset-income field exists. 2) Restricted to race=='black' (n=3,013; ever_jailed=159, 5.3%). 3) Used composite_wealth_1985 as the pre-incarceration proxy for income/economic level and stratified into tertiles (q33=0, q67=3830 -> low/mid/high); verified jailed sub-cells all >=15 (76/39/44) so 3 tiers retained. 4) Computed wealth changes d96=w1996-w1985 (primary, post-window) and d90=w1990-w1985 (aux, mid-window), plus 1996 level. 5) Within each tier compared ever_jailed=1 vs 0 on mean and median, reporting n and using sex as the only simple control; computed the not-jailed-minus-jailed gap. 6) Reported a monotonic pattern: the incarceration-associated wealth shortfall grows with baseline wealth tier. All figures reproducible via analysis.py; summary in results_summary.txt.
